summary: @servicetitan/intl preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime v1.3.13 from GitHub's oven-sh/bun release assets into a temporary directory, extracts and chmods it, then invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a ~728KB single-line heavily obfuscated bundle (rotating numeric string-array with a `WV8StW` shift-decoder, hex-mangled identifiers) that is not referenced by the library's `dist/` entry points and whose name has no relationship to the package's advertised i18n purpose. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated with `_0x...`-style renamed identifiers and per-function string-lookup dictionaries. The alternate-runtime-dropper shape (fetch a second JS runtime and use it to execute an opaque adjacent payload) evades Node-based install-time scanners, and executes automatically on `npm install` via the preinstall lifecycle hook. The package name matches the ServiceTitan npm scope for an internationalization library, consistent with a scope/maintainer compromise pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
